title: Effectiveness of RAG + Deterministic Verifier vs LLM-only for Intent→Configuration Correctness (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does combining retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a deterministic network-configuration verifier and one automated repair iteration reduce the paired critical configuration error rate relative to LLM-only intent→configuration generation across a diverse 200-task set?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The RAG+verifier pipeline reduces the proportion of critical configuration errors (verifier-detected or sandbox-executed reachability/isolation violations per intent) by ≥30% relative to LLM-only (paired within-task comparison).
H2: LLM-only outputs will exhibit a higher rate of syntax/semantic or unsupported-assertion failures (non-executable or verifier-detected semantic errors) than RAG+verifier outputs.

H3: End-to-end latency (model+retrieval+verification) for RAG+verifier will have a higher median than LLM-only by >100 ms, but remain within interactive-tolerance bounds for operator workflows (pre-specified thresholds).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do effect sizes vary by topology family and protocol scenario?
EQ2: How sensitive are results to the choice of hosted LLM (primary vs alternate on a held-out subset)?
EQ3: What failure-mode categories (reachability, isolation, ACL misconfiguration, routing leaks) dominate residual critical errors after RAG+verifier?
benchmark_scope: Constructed public-task corpus (200 intents) drawn from public vendor docs, RFCs, and prior NetOps benchmarks (snapshot indexed; see corpus snapshot hash).
Sandboxed simulation using containerized deterministic network simulator/verifier (Docker-compatible Batfish-style ruleset).
Scope explicitly bounded to syntactic/semantic correctness and reachability/isolation properties in the sandbox; no production deployment claims.
primary_estimand: Paired difference in critical error probability per task: P(LLM-only produces critical error) - P(RAG+verifier produces critical error) (task as clustering unit).
secondary_estimands: Paired difference in non-critical semantic/syntax error rates.
Paired difference in median end-to-end latency (ms).
sampling_plan: Total confirmatory task set = 200 natural-language intents. Composition: 4 topology families × 3 protocol scenarios = 12 cells. Distribution: 8 cells with 17 tasks and 4 cells with 16 tasks (8*17 + 4*16 = 200). An external-validation subset of 40 tasks (20% of 200) is pre-specified and stratified across topology families (10 tasks per family). For each task we execute both pipelines (paired design). Inclusion/exclusion rules, prompts, retrieval-index seeds, and the exact task list will be snapshot-published and hashed prior to execution.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired difference in critical error rate (task-level). Target effect: ≥30% relative reduction (example baseline p0 = 0.40 → target p1 = 0.28; absolute reduction = 0.12). With N=200 tasks and two-sided α=0.05, approximate power ≈ 0.80–0.90 under assumed baseline; exact power calculated using observed discordant counts and reported. If observed baseline is substantially lower, report reduced power and treat results accordingly. Pre-specified sensitivity: recompute power post-hoc and report detectable effect sizes.
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks persistently failing due to infrastructure or API outages after one automatic retry; report exclusions with reasons and counts.
No post-hoc replacement of excluded tasks; all exclusions and reasons published.
missingness_plan: Missing outputs due to infrastructure or API failures are technical failures: re-run once if failure is transient (per preregistered retry policy); if persistent, exclude task and report exclusion counts and reasons. No post-hoc task replacements. Report complete-case and intention-to-run summaries. No human imputation; missingness descriptive only.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary outcome (critical error: yes/no) per task; use McNemar's test for paired binary data (two-sided α=0.05) and report risk difference with 95% CI. Report raw discordant counts (n01,n10), absolute and relative risk reductions, exact p-values. Secondary analyses: Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired latency comparisons; per-topology subgroup analyses pre-specified (4 families). Multiple testing for subgroup/secondary endpoints controlled with Benjamini–Hochberg (FDR 0.05). Robustness: repeated analyses excluding tasks flagged for retrieval-corpus overlap and excluding tasks with ambiguous intent per pre-specified ambiguity score. All code, seeds, prompts, and raw outputs archived.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is a single paired comparison (H1). Secondary and exploratory tests (H2,H3, subgroup analyses) are labeled non-confirmatory; report adjusted p-values for secondary/subgroup tests using Benjamini–Hochberg. No alpha spending beyond the primary test.

stopping_rule: No early scientific stopping for efficacy. Execute all 200 paired tasks. Stop only for persistent systemic infrastructure/provider outage preventing completion within the allotted wall-clock window (7 days) or for catastrophic data-corruption; in such cases abort, report exact failure modes, exclusion counts, and hashes. Transient API failures: one automatic retry per task as per missingness_plan.
